Massive Beams was founded in the heart of Berlin with the vision to become the leading platform for Open RAN Radio Unit (O-RU) development. With the emergence of 5G and 6G on the horizon, the importance of Open RAN - an open specification for how base station components communicate - is growing. This innovation will create an open and transparent marketplace, allowing vendors around the world to bring their cutting-edge solutions to mobile communications.
 
However, the road ahead is not without challenges. Many of the O-RU solutions available today are opaque, difficult to configure and time-consuming to integrate. As we look to future 6G technologies, integrating them into the Open RAN will be even more challenging when the hardware available today is already difficult to operate.
 
This is where Massive Beams comes in. We fill this gap in the market by providing the first modular Open RAN Radio Unit development platform specifically designed to help Open RAN vendors, universities and research institutions focus on their core competencies. Our platform simplifies the integration of innovative future 6G technologies into the Open RAN specifications and enables a rapid transition from development platform to mass production of radio units - from small cells to macro cells - leading the way to the 6G future.
 
We make Open RAN integration easy and provide solutions tailored to your needs.

 Adapting ports to rising sea levels: an economic necessity for the future
As sea levels rise, port infrastructure - whether commercial, fishing or leisure - becomes increasingly vulnerable. Subjected to extreme weather phenomena, these ports, which are essential to the global economy, risk suffering considerable damage if proactive measures are not implemented. As an article in the French newspaper Le Monde points out, ‘the priority now is adaptation rather than inaction’, because the costs of inaction will far outweigh those of adaptation.

Adapt or incur the significant costs of inaction ⚠️
Ports that fail to adapt risk becoming increasingly vulnerable, while those that respond proactively to these challenges will enjoy a considerable competitive advantage. By modernising their port management and integrating cutting-edge technologies such as digital twins and artificial intelligence, they will ensure their competitiveness in the face of escalating climate challenges. Ports that embrace adaptation today will become the leaders of tomorrow.

ABIM: Robust solutions for the cities and ports of the future 
ABIM helps port managers anticipate climate-related challenges. By integrating spatial data (InSAR), digital twins and artificial intelligence technologies, we provide proactive management, predictive maintenance and risk assessment. This enables ports to improve their sustainability and efficiency.

 Anticipate consequences to mitigate expenses
The cost of adaptation is much lower than the cost of inaction. An EDFund report entitled ‘Early or Pay Later’ indicates that the costs of adaptation can be up to 90% lower than the costs of repairing infrastructure following extreme weather events. This approach could result in annual savings of $100 billion for the world's port infrastructures.

Resilient cities and ports are not just an option, they are an essential condition for the future !

AMAREA Technology offers industrial 3D printers and high-performance materials based on Multi Material Jetting (MMJ) technology. We go beyond the limits that the creative freedom of additive manufacturing with a single material offers manufacturers.
MMJ enables printing with different materials, even with contrasting properties, both within the same layer and throughout the build volume. Materials within the same material class, such as metals, ceramics and plastics, or even different material classes, can be integrated into a single build job.
Features and specifications of the technology:
3D printers based on Multi Material Jetting (MMJ) represent an additive manufacturing process in which material is deposited drop by drop and layer by layer.
Each of the MMJ-capable materials is composed of the desired material as a powder embedded in a thermoplastic binder.
A print head contains one material and releases tiny droplets (containing the actual material powder) as required (nl size). The droplets solidify by cooling in a fraction of a second and become solid structures when they reach the build platform or another layer of MMJ-capable material. The neighboring droplets fuse together. Depending on the configuration, several print heads apply different materials drop by drop with high precision throughout the entire build volume.
During the subsequent thermal treatment, known as debinding and sintering, the binder is removed and the remaining material powder particles fuse together to form a solid component and produce the component with the desired properties.

Surrey AI Imaging Limited (SAIIL) is a pioneering technology start-up nestled in the heart of Surrey, UK. SAIIL’s core specialisation lies in the realm of image processing, AI and software engineering, with a pronounced focus on planetary remote sensing and Earth observation. The technical team at SAIIL, led by Dr. Yu Tao as the Technical Director, is a melting pot of talent, innovation, and experience. With a rich tapestry of knowledge in computer vision, remote sensing, geospatial data analytics, VR, GIS, machine learning, and deep learning, SAIIL’s team is adept at devising and implementing image processing algorithms, deep learning models, and their applications to address intricate challenges in planetary and Earth remote sensing. SAIIL’s suite of expertise includes:
· Satellite Imaging: From super-resolution restoration of various resolutions and bands to shadow detection and re-shading using deep learning.
· 3D Reconstruction: Leveraging techniques like photogrammetry, photoclinometry, and structure from motion for topographic mapping and subpixel-scale 3D reconstructions.
· Image Analysis: This encompasses satellite image matching, multi-resolution image co-registration, optical flow-based tracking, and object detection on both Earth and planetary surfaces.
· Data Analytics: SAIIL delves deep into imaging and geospatial data analytics, including effective resolution measurements, multi-spectral statistics, and camera model transformations.
· Optimisation: SAIIL’s team is proficient in GPU optimisations, AI model acceleration, and developing onboard solutions for remote sensing applications, aptly termed "smart-satellite" solutions.

SAIIL's inception and growth have been marked by a series of successful UKSA and ESA funded projects and collaborations. Notably, SAIIL’s association with esteemed institutions like Joanneum Research (Austria), JPL/NASA (U.S.), and University College London (UK) has led to ground-breaking work in the domain of deep learning-based remote sensing techniques, onboard AI solutions, and more.
